subject.title: Add native PowerShell smoke coverage for contributor commands

question: Should the native PowerShell smoke lane include `pnpm build:strict-smoke` now, or start with only commands that are already proven stable on the Windows runner?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible, but the exact recurring CI command set changes Windows runner scope and the active candidate has evidence that one selected command still needs proof or narrowing.

options.title: Prove full smoke before merge
options.body: Keep the requested command set, but merge only after `pnpm check:docs` and `pnpm build:strict-smoke` both pass under Windows `pwsh` with redacted proof.

options.title: Start narrower
options.body: Land native PowerShell coverage for only the commands that already pass, and leave build-smoke coverage to a follow-up.

options.title: Defer runner cost
options.body: Keep the issue open but delay recurring Windows PowerShell smoke coverage until runner budget or release priorities justify it.

recommendation.title: Prove full smoke before merge
recommendation.body: Keep the requested command set, but merge only after `pnpm check:docs` and `pnpm build:strict-smoke` both pass under Windows `pwsh` with redacted proof.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent overlap across CI workflow stabilization and the PowerShell-safe docs tooling adjacent to the requested smoke commands.
